title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description: The unforgettable novel of childhood in a sleepy Southern town and the crisis of conscience that rocked it, exploring compassion and justice through Atticus Finch.

author: George Orwell
description: A chilling dystopian masterpiece depicting the perils of totalitarianism, pervasive surveillance, and the complete destruction of historical truth in Oceania.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: The romantic clash between the opinionated Elizabeth Bennet and her proud aristocratic suitor, Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy, in Georgian England.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description: The brilliant multi-generational chronicle of the mythical town of Macondo through seven generations of the Buendía family, a pinnacle of magical realism.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description: The quintessential American novel of the Jazz Age, charting Jay Gatsby’s desperate pursuit of the elusive Daisy Buchanan against decadent Long Island.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
description: Holden Caulfield’s iconic, poignant three-day odyssey through New York City after expulsion from prep school, confronting adulthood and superficiality.

title: Beloved
author: Toni Morrison
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning hypnotic masterpiece of post-Civil War Ohio, tracing Sethe, an escaped slave haunted physically and emotionally by her past.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphaned young woman’s resilient battle for independence, moral dignity, and passionate love amidst the dark secrets of Thornfield Hall.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: A feverish psychological exploration of guilt, moral redemption, and existential suffering through the impoverished student Raskolnikov in St. Petersburg.

title: Brave New World
author: Aldous Huxley
description: Visionary masterpiece detailing a technologically engineered future world where citizens are genetically graded, conditioned, and drugged with soma.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: A tempestuous, gothic tale of destructive passion, obsession, and vengeance between Catherine Earnshaw and the foundling Heathcliff on the Yorkshire moors.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Oscar Wilde’s philosophical story of aestheticism and moral decadence, where a portrait ages and bears the sins of a young man who remains forever youthful.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
description: A nameless father and his young son journey across a burned, post-apocalyptic America, sustaining humanity and unconditional love amidst ash and ruin.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: The magical allegorical story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of worldly treasure and learns to listen to his heart.

title: Life of Pi
author: Yann Martel
description: An imaginative survival adventure of sixteen-year-old Indian boy Pi Patel stranded on a lifeboat in the Pacific Ocean with a Bengal tiger named Richard Parker.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
description: An unforgettable story of unlikely friendship between an affluent boy and the son of his father’s servant against the tragic backdrop of war-torn Afghanistan.

title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
author: Robert C. Martin
description: Even bad code can function. But if code isn’t clean, it can bring a development organization to its knees. Master meaningful naming, clean functions, and unit testing.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer: 20th Anniversary Edition
author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
description: Illustrates timeless wisdom on software architecture, keeping code flexible, mastering tool automation, avoiding duplication (DRY), and staying pragmatic.

title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
description: The legendary Gang of Four catalog of 23 software architecture patterns providing time-tested object-oriented solutions to recurring engineering problems.

title: Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd Edition
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
description: Comprehensive, rigorous textbook on data structures, algorithmic analysis, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, and graph theory (CLRS).

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
author: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman
description: The classic MIT computer science curriculum text on computational abstraction, functional programming in Scheme, recursion, and metalinguistic abstraction.

title: Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code
author: Martin Fowler
description: Learn how to improve the internal structure and design of existing software without altering its external behavior, with modern JavaScript code examples.

title: Code Complete, 2nd Edition
author: Steve McConnell
description: The quintessential practical guide to software construction, defensive programming, variable naming, quality assurance, and architecture.

title: Effective Java, 3rd Edition
author: Joshua Bloch
description: Joshua Bloch presents 90 indispensable rules of thumb for Java programming, functional paradigms, generics, lambdas, streams, and concurrency.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: An acclaimed tour de force exploring distributed systems, data modeling, replication, partitioning, transactions, consensus, and batch/stream processing.

title: JavaScript: The Good Parts
author: Douglas Crockford
description: Uncovers the elegant subset of JavaScript, exploring functions as first-class objects, lexical scope, prototype inheritance, and JSON data exchange.

title: Working Effectively with Legacy Code
author: Michael C. Feathers
description: Practical strategies for getting large legacy codebases into automated test harnesses safely without breaking existing production behavior.

title: Grokking Algorithms: An Illustrated Guide
author: Aditya Y. Bhargava
description: A fully illustrated, friendly guide that teaches how to apply common algorithms to practical programming problems like search, sorting, and graph algorithms.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
author: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
description: 189 programming interview questions and solutions covering data structures, algorithm problem solving, Big O complexity, and behavioral tactics.

title: The Mythical Man-Month: Essays on Software Engineering
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.
description: Few books on software project management have been as influential and enduring. Articulates Brooks’s Law: adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.

title: Modern Operating Systems, 4th Edition
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Herbert Bos
description: In-depth exploration of modern operating system design, process synchronization, security, Android/Linux kernels, and multicore processor management.

title: Database System Concepts, 7th Edition
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, S. Sudarshan
description: The definitive text on relational databases, SQL queries, transaction management, ACID properties, recovery architectures, and modern NoSQL systems.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description: Set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune tells the story of Paul Atreides as he navigates political betrayal and discovers a profound destiny.

title: Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
description: Hari Seldon uses psychohistory to predict the collapse of the Galactic Empire and creates the Foundation to preserve human civilization.

title: Neuromancer
author: William Gibson
description: The seminal cyberpunk novel following Case, a washed-up computer hacker hired for one last desperate run in the matrix cyberspace.

title: Hyperion
author: Dan Simmons
description: Seven pilgrims journey to the Time Tombs on the mysterious world of Hyperion, each sharing their story while the deadly Shrike awaits.

title: Snow Crash
author: Neal Stephenson
description: In a dystopian Los Angeles, pizza delivery hacker Hiro Protagonist investigates a lethal computer virus that affects hackers in the Metaverse and reality.

title: Ender's Game
author: Orson Scott Card
description: Child genius Ender Wiggin is drafted into an orbital Battle School to train in zero-gravity war games against an impending alien invasion.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick
description: Bounty hunter Rick Deckard is tasked with retiring rogue Nexus-6 androids in a radioactive, dying post-apocalyptic San Francisco.

title: The Left Hand of Darkness
author: Ursula K. Le Guin
description: Human envoy Genly Ai visits the frozen planet Gethen, whose inhabitants can choose and change their gender, exploring duality and communication.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description: Guy Montag is a fireman whose job is to burn forbidden books in a consumerist society obsessed with television walls and sensory overload.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
author: Douglas Adams
description: Arthur Dent is plucked off Earth moments before its demolition by a Vogon constructor fleet, beginning an absurd comedic trek across the cosmos.

title: Rendezvous with Rama
author: Arthur C. Clarke
description: Astronauts explore an immense, hollow cylindrical alien vessel entering the Solar System, encountering unfathomable mysteries.

title: Children of Time
author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
description: Humanity’s dying survivors search for a terraformed planet, only to find it colonized and dominated by an uplifted spider civilization.

title: The Three-Body Problem
author: Cixin Liu
description: Set against the Chinese Cultural Revolution, a secret military project sends signals into space, making contact with an alien civilization on the brink of destruction.

title: Solaris
author: Stanislaw Lem
description: Psychologist Kris Kelvin arrives on a research station orbiting the oceanic planet Solaris, which manifests crew members’ repressed memories into physical form.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
author: Arthur C. Clarke
description: A black monolith discovered on the Moon prompts a deep space voyage to Saturn aboard the Discovery One, accompanied by the supercomputer HAL 9000.

title: Leviathan Wakes
author: James S.A. Corey
description: The Expanse series opener follows ice hauler Jim Holden and detective Joe Miller investigating a missing girl and uncovering a solar-system-wide conspiracy.

title: Good to Great: Why Some Companies Make the Leap and Others Don’t
author: Jim Collins
description: Jim Collins and his research team identify the determinants of great results, including Level 5 Leadership, the Hedgehog Concept, and the Flywheel effect.

title: The Lean Startup: How Today’s Entrepreneurs Use Continuous Innovation
author: Eric Ries
description: A revolutionary approach to launching new companies using rapid experimentation, validated learning, and minimum viable products (MVPs).

title: Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future
author: Peter Thiel, Blake Masters
description: Venture capitalist Peter Thiel explains why creating new technology moves civilization from 0 to 1, creating unique monopolies that shape the future.

title: The Innovator’s Dilemma
author: Clayton M. Christensen
description: The landmark book explaining why outstanding companies can do everything right and still lose their market leadership when faced with disruptive technologies.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
description: Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman explains the two systems that drive the way we think: System 1 (fast, intuitive) and System 2 (slow, deliberative).

title: Principles: Life and Work
author: Ray Dalio
description: Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio shares the unconventional principles that he developed, refined, and used over forty years to achieve unique results.

title: Start with Why: How Great Leaders Inspire Everyone to Take Action
author: Simon Sinek
description: Simon Sinek demonstrates that leaders who have had the greatest influence in the world all think, act, and communicate the exact same way—starting with Why.

title: Shoe Dog: A Memoir by the Creator of Nike
author: Phil Knight
description: Nike founder Phil Knight shares the inside story of the company’s early days as an intrepid start-up and its evolution into one of the world’s most iconic brands.

title: Measure What Matters: How Google, Bono, and the Gates Foundation Rock the World with OKRs
author: John Doerr
description: Legendary venture capitalist John Doerr reveals how the goal-setting system of Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) has helped tech giants achieve 10x growth.

title: Rework
author: Jason Fried, David Heinemeier Hansson
description: The founders of 37signals show how to start and operate small, lean, and profitable businesses without endless meetings, plans, or venture capital.

title: Bad Blood: Secrets and Lies in a Silicon Valley Startup
author: John Carreyrou
description: The gripping investigative account of the breathtaking rise and shocking collapse of Theranos, the multibillion-dollar biotech startup founded by Elizabeth Holmes.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things: Building a Business When There Are No Easy Answers
author: Ben Horowitz
description: Ben Horowitz, cofounder of Andreessen Horowitz, draws on his own story of founding, running, selling, and investing in tech companies to give honest advice.

title: Dare to Lead: Brave Work. Tough Conversations. Whole Hearts.
author: Brené Brown
description: Brené Brown teaches that leadership is not about titles, status, and wielding power, but about recognizing the potential in people and having the courage to grow it.

title: Never Split the Difference: Negotiating As If Your Life Depended On It
author: Chris Voss, Tahl Raz
description: Former FBI international hostage negotiator Chris Voss reveals high-stakes negotiation techniques and emotional intelligence tactics for business and life.

title: Blue Ocean Strategy: How to Create Uncontested Market Space
author: W. Chan Kim, Renée Mauborgne
description: Argues that lasting success comes not from battling competitors in crowded red oceans, but from creating blue oceans of untapped new market spaces.

title: High Output Management
author: Andrew S. Grove
description: Legendary former Intel CEO Andy Grove shares the foundational masterclass on managerial leverage, meetings, production principles, and team motivation.

title: Atomic Habits: An Easy & Proven Way to Build Good Habits & Break Bad Ones
author: James Clear
description: No matter your goals, Atomic Habits offers a proven framework for improving every day by focusing on systems rather than goals.

title: Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World
author: Cal Newport
description: Deep work is the ability to focus without distraction on a cognitively demanding task, a superpower in our increasingly competitive information economy.

title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
author: Stephen R. Covey
description: Presents a holistic, integrated, principle-centered approach for solving personal and professional problems through character ethics.

title: Digital Minimalism: Choosing a Focused Life in a Noisy World
author: Cal Newport
description: A philosophy of technology use in which you focus your online time on a small number of carefully selected activities that support things you value.

title: Make Your Bed: Little Things That Can Change Your Life...And Maybe the World
author: William H. McRaven
description: Admiral William H. McRaven recounts 10 life lessons from Navy SEAL training about perseverance, grit, teamwork, and starting the day with accomplished tasks.

title: Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance
author: Angela Duckworth
description: Psychologist Angela Duckworth shows that the secret to outstanding achievement is not talent, but a special blend of passion and long-term perseverance she calls grit.

title: The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck
author: Mark Manson
description: A cut-through-the-crap guide to surviving everyday life by learning how to choose what truly matters and letting go of everything else.

title: Essentialism: The Disciplined Pursuit of Less
author: Greg McKeown
description: The Way of the Essentialist isn’t about getting more done in less time. It’s about getting only the right things done by eliminating nonessentials.

title: Can’t Hurt Me: Master Your Mind and Defy the Odds
author: David Goggins
description: Navy SEAL David Goggins shares his astonishing life story and reveals that most of us tap into only 40 percent of our true mental and physical capabilities.

title: Four Thousand Weeks: Time Management for Mortals
author: Oliver Burkeman
description: An uplifting, philosophical guide to time and time management, confronting mortality and embracing limitations to choose a meaningful life.

title: The Power of Habit: Why We Do What We Do in Life and Business
author: Charles Duhigg
description: Explores the science behind habit formation, cue-routine-reward neurological loops, and how habits can be changed in individuals, companies, and societies.

title: Show Your Work!: 10 Ways to Share Your Creativity and Get Discovered
author: Austin Kleon
description: A cheerful guide to getting discovered by being generous, sharing your daily creative processes, and letting others into your craft.

title: Steal Like an Artist: 10 Things Nobody Told You About Being Creative
author: Austin Kleon
description: Inspiring manifesto that shows how true creative work builds on the ideas that came before it, remixing and re-imagining them authentically.

title: Feel-Good Productivity: How to Do More of What Matters to You
author: Ali Abdaal
description: Doctor and YouTuber Ali Abdaal reveals how feeling good creates motivation, focus, and sustainable energy, turning productivity into a joyful practice.

title: The Mountain Is You: Transforming Self-Sabotage Into Self-Mastery
author: Brianna Wiest
description: Explores self-sabotage as conflicting needs meeting coping mechanisms, offering actionable steps to overcome internal trauma and build self-mastery.

title: Mindset: The New Psychology of Success
author: Carol S. Dweck
description: World-renowned Stanford psychologist Carol Dweck explains the power of our mindset: fixed mindset limits growth, while growth mindset fosters achievement.

title: The Art of Invisibility: The World’s Most Famous Hacker Teaches You How to Be Safe in the Age of Big Brother
author: Kevin Mitnick
description: Legendary hacker Kevin Mitnick provides a masterclass on protecting privacy, combating digital tracking, understanding encryption, and navigating online surveillance.

title: Practical Malware Analysis: The Hands-On Guide to Dissecting Malicious Software
author: Michael Sikorski, Andrew Honig
description: The definitive hands-on manual for static and dynamic analysis, disassembling binaries with IDA Pro, reverse engineering, and debugging malware.

title: Ghost in the Wires: My Adventures as the World’s Most Wanted Hacker
author: Kevin Mitnick
description: The gripping true crime memoir of Kevin Mitnick as he bypassed telephone networks, penetrated Fortune 500 computer systems, and eluded the FBI.

title: Countdown to Zero Day: Stuxnet and the Launch of the World’s First Digital Weapon
author: Kim Zetter
description: The riveting inside story of Stuxnet, the sophisticated cyberweapon that targeted Iran’s Natanz nuclear enrichment facility and altered military history.

title: This Is How They Tell Me the World Ends: The Cyberweapons Arms Race
author: Nicole Perlroth
description: New York Times reporter Nicole Perlroth investigates the clandestine, multi-billion-dollar global black market for zero-day software exploits.

title: The Web Application Hacker’s Handbook: Finding and Exploiting Security Flaws
author: Dafydd Stuttard, Marcus Pinto
description: The comprehensive guide to web application penetration testing, SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), session fixation, and authentication attacks.

title: Hacking: The Art of Exploitation, 2nd Edition
author: Jon Erickson
description: Introduces the art of hacking from first principles using C, assembly, memory buffers, network sniffers, and cryptographic attacks.

title: Black Hat Python, 2nd Edition: Python Programming for Hackers and Pentesters
author: Justin Seitz, Tim Arnold
description: Practical guide to writing network sniffers, stealing email credentials, bypassing anti-virus software, and executing Trojan command-and-control with Python.

title: Blue Team Handbook: Incident Response Edition
author: Don Murdoch
description: A compact field manual for cybersecurity first responders covering incident triage, volatile memory capture, network forensics, and containment protocols.

title: Threat Modeling: Designing for Security
author: Adam Shostack
description: Practical methodologies for finding system threats during software architecture and design, including STRIDE, threat trees, and risk prioritization.

title: Sandworm: A New Era of Cyberwar and the Hunt for the Kremlin’s Most Dangerous Hackers
author: Andy Greenberg
description: Chronicles the most devastating cyberwarfare attacks in history, tracing the Russian military hacker unit behind BlackEnergy, NotPetya, and the Ukrainian power grid shutdowns.

title: The Tangled Web: A Guide to Securing Modern Web Applications
author: Michal Zalewski
description: Deep dive into the web browser security model, same-origin policy, DOM manipulation, cookie security quirks, and cross-site request forgery.

title: Security Engineering: A Guide to Building Dependable Distributed Systems, 3rd Edition
author: Ross Anderson
description: Ross Anderson’s magnum opus covers cryptology, access control, side-channel attacks, ATM security, nuclear command systems, and social engineering.

title: Cult of the Dead Cow: How the Original Hacking Supergroup Might Just Save the World
author: Joseph Menn
description: The inside history of the legendary hacker collective cDc that invented the Back Orifice remote tool and established the ethical principles of disclosure.

title: Silence on the Wire: A Field Guide to Passive Reconnaissance and Indirect Attacks
author: Michal Zalewski
description: An unconventional look at hardware side channels, packet timing attacks, TCP/IP stack fingerprinting, and acoustic emanations in computer systems.

title: Network Security Assessment: Know Your Network, 3rd Edition
author: Chris McNab
description: A tactical blueprint for assessing IP networks, perimeter firewalls, VPNs, routing protocols, wireless links, and enterprise infrastructure.

title: Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: Bold, provocative exploration of the cognitive, agricultural, and scientific revolutions that shaped Homo sapiens into rulers of planet Earth.

title: Guns, Germs, and Steel: The Fates of Human Societies
author: Jared Diamond
description: Pulitzer Prize winner examining how environmental and geographical factors, rather than racial differences, shaped global civilizations and inequalities.

title: The Silk Roads: A New History of the World
author: Peter Frankopan
description: A breathtaking epic reassessment of world history centering on the heart of Asia, through which trade, culture, religions, and empires arose.

title: A People’s History of the United States
author: Howard Zinn
description: Tells American history from the perspective of workers, women, Native Americans, and minority groups struggling against oppression.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich: A History of Nazi Germany
author: William L. Shirer
description: The monumental, authoritative history of Adolf Hitler’s Germany, documented firsthand by American war correspondent William L. Shirer.

author: David McCullough
description: Master historian David McCullough tells the dramatic story of the American military campaign of 1776 led by General George Washington.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
description: World-renowned classicist Mary Beard investigates how an unremarkable muddy village in central Italy became a superpower spanning three continents.

title: Genghis Khan and the Making of the Modern World
author: Jack Weatherford
description: The shocking true story of how Genghis Khan united nomadic tribes and forged an empire that pioneered paper currency, religious tolerance, and free commerce.

title: The Splendid and the Vile: A Saga of Churchill, Family, and Defiance During the Blitz
author: Erik Larson
description: Erik Larson paints an intimate, thrilling portrait of Winston Churchill and London citizens weathering the Nazi bombing campaign of 1940-1941.

title: The Wright Brothers
author: David McCullough
description: The inspiring dramatic human story of Wilbur and Orville Wright, two bicycle mechanics from Dayton, Ohio, who changed history by inventing mechanical flight.

title: Churchill: Walking with Destiny
author: Andrew Roberts
description: Acclaimed definitive one-volume biography drawn from King George VI’s wartime diaries, capturing Winston Churchill’s flaws, eccentricities, and heroism.

title: The Warmth of Other Suns: The Epic Story of America’s Great Migration
author: Isabel Wilkerson
description: Pulitzer Prize winner Isabel Wilkerson chronicles the six-decade exodus of six million black citizens who fled the South for northern and western cities.

title: Team of Rivals: The Political Genius of Abraham Lincoln
author: Doris Kearns Goodwin
description: A landmark study of Abraham Lincoln’s political mastery in bringing his fiercest rivals into his Civil War cabinet to preserve the American Union.

title: The Looming Tower: Al-Qaeda and the Road to 9/11
author: Lawrence Wright
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning definitive investigation into the historical events and ideological clashes leading to the September 11 terrorist attacks.

title: Band of Brothers: E Company, 506th Regiment, 101st Airborne
author: Stephen E. Ambrose
description: The legendary chronicle of Easy Company’s paratroopers through D-Day, Operation Market Garden, the Battle of the Bulge, and Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest.

title: Alexander Hamilton
author: Ron Chernow
description: The monumental biography of America’s first Treasury Secretary that inspired the Broadway musical, capturing the brilliant orphan who forged the US economy.

title: Outliers: The Story of Success
author: Malcolm Gladwell
description: Malcolm Gladwell investigates the world of high achievers, showing that cultural legacy, timing, and 10,000 hours of deliberate practice matter more than raw IQ.

title: Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can’t Stop Talking
author: Susan Cain
description: Susan Cain argues that we dramatically undervalue introverts, showing how much we lose in culture, leadership, and science by celebrating only the extrovert ideal.

title: Educated: A Memoir
author: Tara Westover
description: Born to survivalists in rural Idaho, Tara Westover set foot in a classroom for the first time at age seventeen and eventually earned a PhD from Cambridge.

title: The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks
author: Rebecca Skloot
description: Her name was Henrietta Lacks, but scientists know her as HeLa. Her cells—harvested without consent—became one of the most vital tools in modern medicine.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
author: Paul Kalanithi
description: At age thirty-six, on the verge of completing a decade’s worth of training as a neurosurgeon, Paul Kalanithi was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. A profound meditation.

title: Into the Wild
author: Jon Krakauer
description: The haunting true story of Christopher McCandless, a young man from a wealthy family who hitchhiked to Alaska and walked alone into the wilderness north of Mt. McKinley.

title: Born a Crime: Stories from a South African Childhood
author: Trevor Noah
description: The compelling, inspiring, and comically candid story of Trevor Noah’s coming of age in South Africa during the twilight of apartheid and its aftermath.

title: The Tipping Point: How Little Things Can Make a Big Difference
author: Malcolm Gladwell
description: Gladwell explores that magic moment when an idea, trend, or social behavior crosses a threshold, tips, and spreads like wildfire across a population.

title: Blink: The Power of Thinking Without Thinking
author: Malcolm Gladwell
description: An artful look at thin-slicing: the instantaneous choices and snap judgments our unconscious minds make in the blink of an eye.

title: Nickel and Dimed: On (Not) Getting By in America
author: Barbara Ehrenreich
description: Journalist Barbara Ehrenreich goes undercover as an entry-level worker to discover whether anyone can truly survive on minimum-wage labor in America.

title: In Cold Blood
author: Truman Capote
description: The pioneering non-fiction novel reconstructing the brutal murder of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas, and the capture and execution of their killers.

title: Midnight in Chernobyl: The Untold Story of the World’s Greatest Nuclear Disaster
author: Adam Higginbotham
description: Definitive, minute-by-minute account of the April 1986 disaster at Chernobyl Power Station Unit 4, based on declassified Soviet archives and survivor accounts.

title: Just Mercy: A Story of Justice and Redemption
author: Bryan Stevenson
description: Equal Justice Initiative founder Bryan Stevenson recounts his legal crusade to defend the poor, wrongly condemned, and vulnerable trapped in the US penal system.

title: The Glass Castle: A Memoir
author: Jeannette Walls
description: A remarkable memoir of resilience and redemption, and a revelatory look into a family at once deeply eccentric and unique in its fierce love.

title: Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly
author: Anthony Bourdain
description: Anthony Bourdain’s wildly entertaining and notoriously frank insider exposé of Manhattan’s culinary world, pirate kitchen crews, and gastronomic obsession.

title: The Devil in the White City: Murder, Magic, and Madness at the Fair That Changed America
author: Erik Larson
description: Interweaves the incredible true tale of Daniel H. Burnham constructing the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair with the chilling exploits of serial killer H. H. Holmes.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: Stephen Hawking explores deep questions about the cosmos: Where did the universe come from? Can time run backward? What lies inside black holes?

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: Carl Sagan retraces 15 billion years of cosmic evolution that transformed matter and life into consciousness, exploring science, wonder, and humanity’s future.

title: The Selfish Gene
author: Richard Dawkins
description: A classic work on evolutionary biology arguing that the gene is the fundamental unit of selection and introducing the concept of the meme.

title: The Gene: An Intimate History
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: A magnificent history of genetics, from Mendel and Darwin to CRISPR gene-editing and the future of human identity and hereditary diseases.

title: The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer
author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
description: Pulitzer Prize winner charting the biological epic of cancer, centuries of discoveries, radical surgical treatments, chemotherapy, and molecular targeted therapy.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
description: Neil deGrasse Tyson breaks down the cosmos into quick, insightful chapters on quantum mechanics, general relativity, dark energy, and cosmic expansion.

title: What If?: Serious Scientific Answers to Absurd Hypothetical Questions
author: Randall Munroe
description: The creator of xkcd answers bizarre hypothetical questions—from relativistic baseballs to draining the oceans—using rigorous physics equations and humor.

title: The Demon-Haunted World: Science as a Candle in the Dark
author: Carl Sagan
description: Carl Sagan’s passionate defense of scientific thinking, empirical skepticism, and the baloney detection kit against superstition and pseudoscience.

title: Reality Is Not What It Seems: The Journey to Quantum Gravity
author: Carlo Rovelli
description: Theoretical physicist Carlo Rovelli guides us through loop quantum gravity, showing how space and time dissolve into a granular web at Planck scales.

title: The Order of Time
author: Carlo Rovelli
description: A lyrical, mind-bending exploration of the physics and philosophy of time, showing why time does not flow universally or exist as we intuitively assume.

title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
author: Carlo Rovelli
description: A delightful introduction to modern physics covering Einstein’s general relativity, quantum mechanics, elementary particles, black holes, and the universe.

title: The Seven Daughters of Eve: The Science That Reveals Our Genetic Ancestry
author: Bryan Sykes
description: Oxford geneticist Bryan Sykes reveals how mitochondrial DNA tracing links 99 percent of modern native Europeans to just seven prehistoric clan mothers.

title: The Sixth Extinction: An Unnatural History
author: Elizabeth Kolbert
description: Pulitzer Prize winner examining how human industrial activity is precipitating a mass extinction event comparable to the asteroid impact that wiped out dinosaurs.

title: Genome: The Autobiography of a Species in 23 Chapters
author: Matt Ridley
description: Matt Ridley picks one newly discovered gene from each of the 23 pairs of human chromosomes to tell the dramatic story of human evolution and health.

title: The Hidden Life of Trees: What They Feel, How They Communicate
author: Peter Wohlleben
description: Forester Peter Wohlleben shares groundbreaking scientific discoveries about the social networks of trees, underground fungal wood-wide webs, and mutual care.

title: Entangled Life: How Fungi Make Our Worlds, Change Our Minds & Shape Our Futures
author: Merlin Sheldrake
description: Biologist Merlin Sheldrake takes us on an astonishing journey into fungi, the organism network that links forests, breaks down pollutants, and shapes all life.

title: The Innovators: How a Group of Hackers, Geniuses, and Geeks Created the Digital Revolution
author: Walter Isaacson
description: From Ada Lovelace and Alan Turing to Bill Gates and Steve Jobs, Isaacson reveals how collaborative geniuses created the computer, microchip, and internet.

title: Life 3.0: Being Human in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
author: Max Tegmark
description: MIT professor Max Tegmark explores how artificial intelligence will affect crime, war, justice, jobs, society, and our very sense of being human.

title: Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies
author: Nick Bostrom
description: Oxford philosopher Nick Bostrom maps out the monumental existential challenge humankind will face when machine intelligence exceeds human biological intellect.

title: AI Superpowers: China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order
author: Kai-Fu Lee
description: Dr. Kai-Fu Lee reveals how unexpected developments in AI will dramatically accelerate the global economic battle between the US and China.

title: The Soul of a New Machine
author: Tracy Kidder
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning classic account of the feverish race by a team of Data General engineers to build a revolutionary 32-bit superminicomputer.

title: Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution
author: Steven Levy
description: Steven Levy’s classic history traces the original computer hackers from the late 1950s MIT laboratories to early homebrew PCs and the gaming revolution.

title: The Master Switch: The Rise and Fall of Information Empires
author: Tim Wu
description: Columbia law professor Tim Wu shows how every major communications technology—telephone, radio, cinema, television—opened freely only to become centralized monopolies.

title: The Alignment Problem: Machine Learning and Human Values
author: Brian Christian
description: A compelling portrait of the growing movement within AI research to align deep reinforcement learning and algorithmic decision systems with human values.

title: You Look Like a Thing and I Love You: How Artificial Intelligence Works
author: Janelle Shane
description: Hilarious, cartoon-filled, and technically accurate guide to how neural networks learn, make hilarious blunders, and reflect training data quirks.

title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism: The Fight for a Human Future at the New Frontier of Power
author: Shoshana Zuboff
description: Harvard professor Shoshana Zuboff exposes how tech monopolies claim human behavioral experience as free raw material for behavioral futures markets.

title: Permanent Record
author: Edward Snowden
description: Edward Snowden shares his personal journey from government contractor to whistleblower who exposed global mass surveillance by the NSA and Five Eyes.

title: Chip War: The Fight for the World’s Most Critical Technology
author: Chris Miller
description: Financial Times Best Business Book of the Year detailing the geopolitical contest between world superpowers over semiconductor microchips and fabrication fabs.

title: The Attention Merchants: The Epic Scramble to Get Inside Our Heads
author: Tim Wu
description: Tim Wu examines the historical monetization of human consciousness, from early newspaper advertising to social media feeds engineering dopamine loops.

title: Weapons of Math Destruction: How Big Data Increases Inequality and Threatens Democracy
author: Cathy O’Neil
description: Mathematician and data scientist Cathy O’Neil reveals how mathematical models used in credit scoring, policing, and hiring reinforce biases while escaping oversight.

title: Algorithms of Oppression: How Search Engines Reinforce Racism
author: Safiya Umoja Noble
description: Safiya Umoja Noble explores how commercial search engine design biases perpetuate racial stereotypes and institutional inequality.

title: The Code: Silicon Valley and the Remaking of America
author: Margaret O’Mara
description: Historian Margaret O’Mara provides the definitive narrative history of Silicon Valley, illuminating the intersection of university research, federal money, and tech capitalism.

title: The Psychology of Money: Timeless Lessons on Wealth, Greed, and Happiness
author: Morgan Housel
description: Morgan Housel shares 19 short stories exploring the strange ways people think about money and teaches you how to make better sense of financial behavior.

title: The Intelligent Investor, Revised Edition
author: Benjamin Graham
description: The greatest investment advisor of the twentieth century, Benjamin Graham, teaches value investing, margin of safety, and emotional discipline against Mr. Market.

title: A Random Walk Down Wall Street: The Time-Tested Strategy for Successful Investing
author: Burton G. Malkiel
description: Burton Malkiel’s established classic on efficient markets, asset allocation, indexing, and behavioral finance for individual long-term investors.

title: One Up On Wall Street: How to Use What You Already Know to Make Money in the Market
author: Peter Lynch
description: Legendary Fidelity Magellan fund manager Peter Lynch explains how average investors can beat Wall Street professionals by paying attention to everyday products.

title: The Millionaire Next Door: The Surprising Secrets of America’s Wealthy
author: Thomas J. Stanley, William D. Danko
description: Identifies common traits among those who have accumulated wealth: living well below means, allocating time and money efficiently, and prioritizing financial independence.

title: I Will Teach You to Be Rich, 2nd Edition
author: Ramit Sethi
description: A no-guilt, no-excuses 6-week personal finance program that shows you how to automate your money, negotiate fees, and spend extravagantly on what you love.

title: The Simple Path to Wealth: Your Road Map to Financial Independence
author: JL Collins
description: Based on his famed letters to his daughter, JL Collins demystifies investing into a simple, ultra-low-cost index fund strategy for financial freedom.

title: Your Money or Your Life: 9 Steps to Transforming Your Relationship with Money
author: Vicki Robin, Joe Dominguez
description: The foundational philosophy of the FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) movement, teaching you to calculate real hourly wages and achieve fulfillment.

title: Rich Dad’s CASHFLOW Quadrant: Rich Dad’s Guide to Financial Freedom
author: Robert T. Kiyosaki
description: Explains the four quadrants: Employee, Self-employed, Business owner, and Investor, and how to shift towards generating passive wealth.

title: Flash Boys: A Wall Street Revolt
author: Michael Lewis
description: Michael Lewis tells the gripping story of high-frequency algorithmic traders rigging modern equity markets and the group of rebels who founded IEX.

title: The Big Short: Inside the Doomsday Machine
author: Michael Lewis
description: The real-life story of the eccentric contrarian investors who foresaw the catastrophic US subprime housing collapse and bet against Wall Street banks.

title: Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits
author: Philip A. Fisher
description: Warren Buffett’s other great mentor, Philip Fisher, presents his fifteen-point checklist for identifying outstanding growth companies with lasting economic moats.

title: The Essays of Warren Buffett: Lessons for Corporate America
author: Lawrence A. Cunningham
description: A curated compilation of Warren Buffett’s annual letters to Berkshire Hathaway shareholders, synthesizing his management and capital allocation wisdom.

title: Liar’s Poker: Rising Through the Wreckage on Wall Street
author: Michael Lewis
description: Michael Lewis’s wild, hilarious memoir of working as a bond salesman on the Salomon Brothers trading floor in the swaggering, reckless 1980s.

title: Against the Gods: The Remarkable Story of Risk
author: Peter L. Bernstein
description: Chronicles the intellectual history of probability, risk measurement, game theory, and derivatives that transformed our understanding of financial markets.

title: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing: The Only Way to Guarantee Your Fair Share of Stock Market Returns
author: John C. Bogle
description: Vanguard founder Jack Bogle explains the mathematical inevitability of low-cost broad-market index investing over actively managed funds.

title: Steve Jobs
author: Walter Isaacson
description: Based on more than forty interviews with Jobs conducted over two years, this is the unvarnished, riveting biography of the creative genius who transformed six industries.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson
description: He was history’s most creative genius. Walter Isaacson weaves Leonardo da Vinci’s art with his notebook discoveries in anatomy, hydraulics, and optics.

title: Elon Musk
author: Walter Isaacson
description: The astonishingly intimate story of the most fascinating and controversial innovator of our era, who led the world into electric vehicles, reusable rocketry, and satellite internet.

title: Becoming
author: Michelle Obama
description: A deeply personal memoir by the former First Lady of the United States, chronicling the experiences that shaped her from the South Side of Chicago to the White House.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: The unforgettable, luminous diary kept by Anne Frank while she and her family were in hiding from the Gestapo in an Amsterdam secret annex.

title: A Promised Land
author: Barack Obama
description: A riveting, deeply personal account of history in the making from the 44th President of the United States, tracing his journey from community organizer to the Oval Office.

title: Long Walk to Freedom: The Autobiography of Nelson Mandela
author: Nelson Mandela
description: The exhilarating autobiography of Nelson Mandela, moving from his youth and twenty-seven years of imprisonment on Robben Island to the triumph of democratic South Africa.

title: Einstein: His Life and Universe
author: Walter Isaacson
description: How did Albert Einstein’s mind work? What made him a genius? Isaacson explores the rebellious patent clerk whose fierce imagination revolutionized our understanding of space and time.

title: Benjamin Franklin: An American Life
author: Walter Isaacson
description: The witty, engrossing biography of the Founding Father who was also America’s first great scientist, diplomat, writer, and quintessential self-made Renaissance man.

title: Open: An Autobiography
author: Andre Agassi
description: One of the most captivating sports autobiographies ever written, capturing Andre Agassi’s secret loathing of tennis, brutal training, and emotional redemption.

title: Born to Run
author: Bruce Springsteen
description: Bruce Springsteen writes with devastating honesty about growing up Catholic in Freehold, New Jersey, the poetry of rock ’n’ roll, and conquering internal darkness.

title: Frida: A Biography of Frida Kahlo
author: Hayden Herrera
description: The lavish biography of the extraordinary Mexican painter Frida Kahlo, detailing her horrific bus accident, tumultuous marriage to Diego Rivera, and brilliant surrealist art.

title: Churchill: A Life
author: Martin Gilbert
description: Sir Martin Gilbert, Churchill’s official biographer, condenses his exhaustive multi-volume masterpiece into an authoritative one-volume life of the wartime British leader.

title: John Adams
author: David McCullough
description: Pulitzer Prize-winning biography of the fiercely independent New England patriot who championed American independence and served as our second president.

title: I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings
author: Maya Angelou
description: Maya Angelou’s poetic and powerful autobiography of abandonment, racial bigotry, trauma, and the liberating wonder of literature and self-expression.

title: Greenlights
author: Matthew McConaughey
description: Academy Award winner Matthew McConaughey shares unconventional wisdom, bumper stickers, failures, and lessons from thirty-five years of journaling on living with purpose.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
author: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
description: Csikszentmihalyi’s seminal investigations into optimal human experience, explaining how flow—a state of deep immersion and concentrated enjoyment—leads to true satisfaction.

title: Predictably Irrational, Revised and Expanded Edition: The Hidden Forces That Shape Our Decisions
author: Dan Ariely
description: Behavioral economist Dan Ariely overturns conventional economic assumptions, showing how irrational behaviors are systematic and predictable.

title: The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma
author: Bessel van der Kolk
description: A preeminent neuroscientist reveals how trauma literally reshapes both body and brain, exploring neuroplasticity, mindfulness, and somatic therapies for healing.

title: Stumbling on Happiness
author: Daniel Gilbert
description: Harvard psychologist Daniel Gilbert describes the shortcomings of our imagination and our cognitive illusions when predicting what will make us happy in the future.

title: Man and His Symbols
author: Carl G. Jung
description: Carl Jung’s only popular work explaining his psychological insights into archetypes, dreams, collective unconscious symbols, and the path to individuation.

title: The Lucifer Effect: Understanding How Good People Turn Evil
author: Philip Zimbardo
description: Stanford Prison Experiment architect Philip Zimbardo analyzes situational power, systemic forces, and institutional roles that cause ordinary people to commit evil.

title: Attached: The New Science of Adult Attachment and How It Can Help You Find—and Keep—Love
author: Amir Levine, Rachel Heller
description: Discover how attachment theory applies to modern relationships, categorizing romantic dynamics into secure, anxious, and avoidant styles.

title: The Antidote: Happiness for People Who Can’t Stand Positive Thinking
author: Oliver Burkeman
description: Explores the negative path to happiness, examining how embracing failure, uncertainty, and mortality provides greater tranquility than toxic positivity.

title: Behave: The Biology of Humans at Our Best and Worst
author: Robert M. Sapolsky
description: Stanford neurobiologist Robert Sapolsky examines human behavior across nested timescales: from milliseconds before an action to sensory inputs, hormones, and evolution.

title: Maybe You Should Talk to Someone: A Therapist, HER Therapist, and Our Lives Revealed
author: Lori Gottlieb
description: Psychotherapist Lori Gottlieb takes us behind the scenes of her therapy practice and her own therapist’s couch, offering wisdom on vulnerability and connection.

title: Thinking in Bets: Making Smarter Decisions When You Don’t Have All the Facts
author: Annie Duke
description: World Series of Poker champion Annie Duke teaches how to separate decision quality from luck, embrace uncertainty, and eliminate resulting bias.

title: The Elephant in the Brain: Hidden Motives in Everyday Life
author: Kevin Simler, Robin Hanson
description: An unflinching investigation into our unacknowledged evolutionary motives in healthcare, education, art, politics, and social signaling.

title: Mistakes Were Made (but Not by Me): Why We Justify Foolish Beliefs, Bad Decisions, and Hurtful Acts
author: Carol Tavris, Elliot Aronson
description: Social psychologists explain cognitive dissonance, confirmation bias, and self-justification, showing how we protect our self-esteem by lying to ourselves.

title: Emotional Intelligence: Why It Can Matter More Than IQ
author: Daniel Goleman
description: Daniel Goleman reveals the neurological insights of emotional intelligence (EQ)—self-awareness, impulse control, empathy, and social dexterity—in determining success.

title: Learned Optimism: How to Change Your Mind and Your Life
author: Martin E.P. Seligman
description: The father of positive psychology explains how explanatory styles dictate resilience and teaches practical cognitive behavioral habits to overcome pessimism.

title: Switch: How to Change Things When Change Is Hard
author: Chip Heath, Dan Heath
description: The Heath brothers show how to guide the Rider (rational mind), motivate the Elephant (emotional mind), and shape the Path to achieve lasting organizational change.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
description: The private spiritual notebook of the Roman Emperor Marcus Aurelius, offering timeless Stoic exercises on duty, acceptance of mortality, and emotional clarity.

title: Letters from a Stoic
author: Seneca
description: Lucius Annaeus Seneca’s letters to his friend Lucilius advising on friendship, grief, poverty, self-reliance, anger, and the brevity of mortal existence.

title: Discourses and Selected Writings
author: Epictetus
description: Born a slave, Epictetus became one of antiquity’s most influential thinkers. Master what is within your control and cultivate inner tranquility.

title: The Republic
author: Plato
description: Socrates and his interlocutors investigate justice, the ideal governance of the city-state, the Allegory of the Cave, and the nature of the philosopher king.

title: Beyond Good and Evil: Prelude to a Philosophy of the Future
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: Friedrich Nietzsche tears down traditional dogmatic morality, unveiling will to power, master-slave morality, and the challenge of the free spirit.

title: The Myth of Sisyphus and Other Essays
author: Albert Camus
description: Albert Camus confronts the Absurd: the fundamental conflict between humanity’s search for inherent meaning and the cold, silent indifference of the universe.

title: The Stranger
author: Albert Camus
description: Through the iconic character Meursault, Albert Camus delivers an indelible fictional exploration of human alienation, absurdity, and truthfulness.

title: Nicomachean Ethics
author: Aristotle
description: Aristotle’s foundational treatise on ethics, eudaimonia (human flourishing), the golden mean of moral virtues, and the cultivation of character.

title: Being and Time
author: Martin Heidegger
description: One of the most profound and influential philosophical works of the twentieth century, analyzing Dasein (Being-in-the-world) and authentic existence.

title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
description: Wittgenstein’s revolutionary logical-philosophical proposition on the limits of language and reality: Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent.

title: The Daily Stoic: 366 Meditations on Wisdom, Perseverance, and the Art of Living
author: Ryan Holiday, Stephen Hanselman
description: A page-a-day guide offering fresh translations and practical modern reflections on the classic teachings of Marcus Aurelius, Seneca, and Epictetus.

title: Justice: What’s the Right Thing to Do?
author: Michael J. Sandel
description: Harvard political philosopher Michael Sandel takes readers on a journey through moral dilemmas, utilitarianism, Kantian duty, and the common good.

title: Critique of Pure Reason
author: Immanuel Kant
description: Kant’s transcendental idealism synthesizes rationalism and empiricism, establishing synthetic a priori knowledge and the cognitive architecture of experience.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: Machiavelli’s notorious classic of political realism, arguing that statecraft often requires practical ruthlessness, prudence, and mastery of fortune over ideal morality.

title: Tao Te Ching
author: Lao Tzu
description: The ancient foundational text of Taoism, providing 81 poetic verses on wu wei (effortless action), humility, simplicity, and living in balance with nature.

title: A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy
author: William B. Irvine
description: Philosopher William B. Irvine shows how ancient Stoic psychological techniques like negative visualization and voluntary discomfort foster deep, lasting joy.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
description: Connell and Marianne grow up in the same small Irish town, but the similarities end there. A magnetic exploration of social class, vulnerability, and intimacy.

title: Red, White & Royal Blue
author: Casey McQuiston
description: When the First Son of the United States falls into a feigned friendship with Britain’s Prince Henry, an unexpected secret romance blossoms that could upend international diplomacy.

title: The Song of Achilles
author: Madeline Miller
description: A breathtakingly lyrical retelling of Homer’s Iliad that follows the deep, passionate bond between the exiled prince Patroclus and the golden hero Achilles.

title: Circe
author: Madeline Miller
description: In the house of Helios, god of the sun, Circe discovers her power of sorcery and chooses human connection and mortal love over the callousness of the gods.

title: Beach Read
author: Emily Henry
description: Two rival authors—a romance writer who stopped believing in love and a brooding literary novelist—swap genres for the summer with hilarious and heartwarming results.

title: Book Lovers
author: Emily Henry
description: Cutthroat literary agent Nora Stephens keeps bumping into brooding Manhattan editor Charlie Lastra in a picturesque North Carolina small town.

title: People We Meet on Vacation
author: Emily Henry
description: Two best friends who couldn’t be more different take one last summer week vacation together to fix a misunderstanding that broke their friendship.

title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: Aging and reclusive Old Hollywood movie icon Evelyn Hugo is finally ready to tell the truth about her glamorous and scandalous life, and her one true great love.

title: Outlander
author: Diana Gabaldon
description: Scottish Highlands, 1945. Claire Randall, a former combat nurse, touches a standing stone circle and is hurled back in time to 1743 into the arms of highland warrior Jamie Fraser.

title: The Love Hypothesis
author: Ali Hazelwood
description: When third-year Ph.D. candidate Olive Smith kisses the first man she sees—who happens to be notorious young biology professor Adam Carlsen—a fake-dating experiment ensues.

title: Daisy Jones & The Six
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: An oral history of the rise and fall of a legendary 1970s rock band fronted by Daisy Jones and Billy Dunne, whose magnetic chemistry ignited fame and heartbreak.

title: One Day
author: David Nicholls
description: Dexter and Emma meet on the night of their university graduation. Where will they be on this one ordinary day—July 15th—over the next twenty years?

title: Call Me by Your Name
author: André Aciman
description: The story of a sudden and powerful romance that blossoms between an adolescent American-Italian boy and a visiting guest scholar on the Italian Riviera.

title: Eleanor & Park
author: Rainbow Rowell
description: Set over the course of one school year in 1986 Omaha, two star-crossed sixteen-year-olds find solace in punk rock cassettes, comic books, and first love.

title: It Happened One Summer
author: Tessa Bailey
description: A Hollywood wild child is cut off from her family wealth and banished to a Pacific Northwest coastal town, where she locks horns with a gruff sea captain.

title: Love and Other Words
author: Christina Lauren
description: The story of Macy and Elliot, childhood sweethearts whose bond fell apart a decade earlier and who are reunited unexpectedly by chance in a coffee shop.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description: Ten strangers are lured to an isolated mansion on an island off Devon coast by a mysterious host, where they are executed one by one according to a nursery rhyme.

title: Murder on the Orient Express
author: Agatha Christie
description: Just after midnight, a snowdrift stops the Orient Express in its tracks. By morning, an American tycoon lies dead in his locked compartment, stabbed a dozen times.

title: The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
author: Agatha Christie
description: The sensational mystery that established Agatha Christie’s reputation, featuring Hercule Poirot investigating a wealthy widow’s blackmailer and an astonishing plot twist.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. John Watson investigate the spectral, fiery-eyed phantom hound said to haunt Dartmoor and plague generations of the Baskerville family.

title: A Study in Scarlet
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: The legendary first appearance of Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson at 221B Baker Street, investigating a murder inscribed with the German word RACHE.

title: The Big Sleep
author: Raymond Chandler
description: Private eye Philip Marlowe enters the corrupt, sun-baked streets of Los Angeles to solve a blackmail case involving the daughters of General Sternwood.

title: The Maltese Falcon
author: Dashiell Hammett
description: Hardboiled detective Sam Spade is drawn into a web of murder and deceit by an eccentric rogues’ gallery pursuing a priceless jewel-encrusted falcon statuette.

title: In the Woods
author: Tana French
description: Detective Rob Ryan investigates the murder of a twelve-year-old girl in the Dublin suburb of Knocknaree, a town where his own childhood friends vanished twenty years before.

title: The Likeness
author: Tana French
description: Detective Cassie Maddox goes undercover to impersonate a murdered university student who looked exactly like her, living among four close-knit graduate suspects.

title: The Maid: A Novel
author: Nita Prose
description: Molly Gray is an eccentric hotel maid who finds notorious real estate tycoon Charles Black dead in his suite, and must rely on true friends to clear her name.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
author: Richard Osman
description: Four retirees in a peaceful retirement village meet weekly to investigate unsolved crimes, but find themselves in the middle of a live murder case right on their doorstep.

title: The Man Who Died Twice
author: Richard Osman
description: The second Thursday Murder Club mystery follows Elizabeth and her sleuthing friends as they untangle an espionage puzzle involving stolen diamonds and mafia assassins.

title: Magpie Murders
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: Editor Susan Ryeland reads the manuscript of bestselling author Alan Conway’s latest whodunit, only to realize the final chapter is missing and Conway is dead.

title: Moonflower Murders
author: Anthony Horowitz
description: Retired publisher Susan Ryeland is asked to investigate the disappearance of a hotel owner’s daughter who claimed a murder described in a mystery novel had actually occurred.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: Alicia Berenson’s life is seemingly perfect until she shoots her husband five times in the face and never speaks another word. Psychotherapist Theo Faber tries to uncover her motive.

title: Truly Devious
author: Maureen Johnson
description: Stevie Bell enters Ellingham Academy, a Vermont boarding school for gifted youths, determined to solve the notorious 1930s kidnapping case of the school founder’s family.

title: Gone Girl
author: Gillian Flynn
description: On their fifth wedding anniversary, Amy Dunne suddenly disappears from their Missouri home. Under intense police and media pressure, husband Nick’s lies begin unraveling.

title: Sharp Objects
author: Gillian Flynn
description: Fresh from a brief stay at a psych hospital, journalist Camille Preaker faces an assignment back in her tiny hometown to cover the unsolved murders of two young girls.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
description: Disgraced journalist Mikael Blomkvist and genius punk hacker Lisbeth Salander uncover dark family corruption and sadistic murders in rural Sweden.

title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
author: Stieg Larsson
description: Lisbeth Salander is framed for three murders in Stockholm, forcing Mikael Blomkvist to race against police to prove her innocence and uncover a sinister conspiracy.

title: The Girl Who Kicked the Hornet’s Nest
author: Stieg Larsson
description: In the thrilling Millennium trilogy finale, Lisbeth Salander battles from an intensive care hospital room to expose corruption at the highest levels of Swedish intelligence.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
description: Symbologist Robert Langdon and cryptologist Sophie Neveu unravel clues hidden in Leonardo da Vinci’s artworks while fleeing Opus Dei and the French police.

title: Angels & Demons
author: Dan Brown
description: When a physicist at CERN is murdered and a canister of antimatter stolen, Robert Langdon races across Rome and the Vatican to stop the vengeance of the Illuminati.

title: Shutter Island
author: Dennis Lehane
description: U.S. Marshal Teddy Daniels investigates the escape of a multiple murderess from Ashecliffe Hospital for the Criminally Insane on an isolated, storm-swept island.

title: Mystic River
author: Dennis Lehane
description: When the nineteen-year-old daughter of ex-con Jimmy Marcus is murdered in Boston, childhood friends turned cop and traumatized suspect are reunited in tragedy.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
author: Thomas Harris
description: FBI trainee Clarice Starling interviews incarcerated psychopathic psychiatrist Dr. Hannibal Lecter to gain psychological insight into serial killer Buffalo Bill.

title: Red Dragon
author: Thomas Harris
description: Retired FBI profiler Will Graham is brought back to hunt the Tooth Fairy, a terrifying serial killer, consulting his nemesis Dr. Hannibal Lecter for psychological clues.

title: Before I Go to Sleep
author: S.J. Watson
description: Christine Lucas wakes every morning with her memory wiped clean. As she secretly keeps a journal, she discovers that the man claiming to be her husband is not telling the truth.

title: The Woman in the Window
author: A.J. Finn
description: Anna Fox is an agoraphobic recluse in her Harlem brownstone who watches neighbors from her window and witnesses an unspeakable crime in the house across the park.

title: Behind Closed Doors
author: B.A. Paris
description: Jack and Grace appear to be the perfect couple with wealth and charm. But Grace is never seen alone without Jack, and steel security shutters cover the downstairs windows.

title: Local Woman Missing
author: Mary Kubica
description: A quiet suburban community is shocked when a mother and her six-year-old daughter vanish. Eleven years later, the girl returns alone, revealing terrifying secrets.

title: The Guest List
author: Lucy Foley
description: Guests gather on a windswept island off the Irish coast for the wedding of a handsome TV star and an ambitious magazine publisher, until a corpse is found as a storm cuts power.

title: The Hobbit
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Bilbo Baggins is a respectable hobbit who is swept into an epic quest by Gandalf the wizard and thirteen dwarves to reclaim the Lonely Mountain from the dragon Smaug.

title: The Fellowship of the Ring: Being the First Part of The Lord of the Rings
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: Frodo Baggins inherits the One Ring of the Dark Lord Sauron and embarks with the Fellowship on an epic journey to Mount Doom to destroy it in the fires of Mordor.

title: The Two Towers: Being the Second Part of The Lord of the Rings
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The Fellowship is broken. Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli battle at Helm’s Deep while Frodo and Sam are guided toward Mordor by the wretched Gollum.

title: The Return of the King: Being the Third Part of The Lord of the Rings
author: J.R.R. Tolkien
description: The climactic final confrontation at the Pelennor Fields and the Black Gate, culminating in the fate of Middle-earth at the cracks of Mount Doom.

title: The Name of the Wind: The Kingkiller Chronicle Day One
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: Kvothe narrates his legendary youth: an orphaned troupe performer, a beggar in Tarbean, and a gifted student learning sympathy and naming at the University.

title: The Wise Man’s Fear: The Kingkiller Chronicle Day Two
author: Patrick Rothfuss
description: Kvothe journeys beyond the University into the court of the Maer Alveron, encounters the Fae realm, and trains in swordplay with the Adem mercenaries.

title: The Way of Kings: The Stormlight Archive Book One
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: On the shattered plains of Roshar, Kaladin Stormblessed leads a condemned bridge crew while highprince Dalinar Kholin experiences visions of the ancient Knights Radiant.

title: Words of Radiance: The Stormlight Archive Book Two
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: The Knights Radiant must be refounded as the Everstorm looms and the Parshendi gamble everything in a desperate clash of Voidbringers.

title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: In a world where ash falls and the Lord Ruler has reigned for a thousand years, a charismatic thief named Kelsier recruits street orphan Vin to execute an impossible heist.

title: The Well of Ascension: Mistborn Book Two
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: They did the impossible by overthrowing the Lord Ruler. Now Vin and Elend Venture must defend Luthadel against three besieging armies and an ancient entity.

title: The Hero of Ages: Mistborn Book Three
author: Brandon Sanderson
description: The monumental culmination of the Mistborn trilogy as Ruin seeks the destruction of Scadrial and Vin discovers the true identity of the Hero of Ages.

title: A Game of Thrones: A Song of Ice and Fire Book One
author: George R.R. Martin
description: Winter is coming. Lord Eddard Stark travels to King’s Landing as Hand of the King while dynastic civil war erupts across Westeros for the Iron Throne.

title: A Clash of Kings: A Song of Ice and Fire Book Two
author: George R.R. Martin
description: Five rival kings contest the Iron Throne in a war of devastation, sorcery, and wildfire, culminating in the epic siege of King’s Landing at the Blackwater.

title: The Blade Itself: The First Law Book One
author: Joe Abercrombie
description: Grimdark masterpiece following the crippled torturer Inquisitor Glokta, barbarian Logen Ninefingers, and nobleman Jezal dan Luthar amidst the schemes of the First of the Magi.

title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
author: Samantha Shannon
description: An extraordinary standalone epic of a divided world where an unwed queen, dragonrider, and mages must unite to prevent the awakening of the Nameless One.

title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
author: Scott Lynch
description: In the Venetian-inspired city of Camorr, Locke Lamora leads the Gentlemen Bastards in audacious confidence heists against corrupt nobility until a shadowy coup strikes.

title: Make It Stick: The Science of Successful Learning
author: Peter C. Brown, Henry L. Roediger III, Mark A. McDaniel
description: Draws on cognitive psychology to demonstrate that retrieval practice, spaced repetition, and interleaving produce far superior retention than rereading or cramming.

title: Why Don’t Students Like School?: A Cognitive Scientist Answers Questions About How the Mind Works
author: Daniel T. Willingham
description: Cognitive scientist Daniel Willingham applies neuroscience and psychology to classroom teaching, explaining memory, curiosity, and effective learning design.

title: How Children Succeed: Grit, Curiosity, and the Hidden Power of Character
author: Paul Tough
description: Argues that the qualities that matter most to children’s success have more to do with non-cognitive skills: perseverance, optimism, and self-control.

title: The Courage to Teach: Exploring the Inner Landscape of a Teacher’s Life
author: Parker J. Palmer
description: Explores the inner life of educators, arguing that good teaching cannot be reduced to technique, but comes from the identity and integrity of the teacher.

title: Teach Like a Champion 3.0: 63 Techniques That Put Students on the Path to College
author: Doug Lemov
description: A practical, concrete instructional handbook detailing 63 actionable techniques observed in the classrooms of high-performing teachers.

title: Visible Learning for Teachers: Maximizing Impact on Learning
author: John Hattie
description: Synthesizes over 900 meta-analyses involving millions of students to establish empirical effect sizes for instructional feedback and formative evaluation.

title: Pedagogy of the Oppressed
author: Paulo Freire
description: The foundational text of critical pedagogy, critiquing the banking model of education and proposing dialogical problem-posing education for human liberation.

title: Mindstorms: Children, Computers, And Powerful Ideas
author: Seymour Papert
description: MIT mathematician and Logo programming creator Seymour Papert presents constructionist learning, showing how computers empower children to learn thinking.

title: Experience and Education
author: John Dewey
description: John Dewey’s concise statement of progressive education, balancing traditional curricula with experiential hands-on student-centered discovery.

title: The Smartest Kids in the World: And How They Got That Way
author: Amanda Ripley
description: Investigates education systems in Finland, South Korea, and Poland through the eyes of American exchange students to see what creates academic excellence.

title: Culturally Responsive Teaching and The Brain
author: Zaretta Hammond
description: Synthesizes neuroscience with culturally responsive teaching to help underserved students build independent learning stamina and intellectual capacity.

title: Small Teaching: Everyday Lessons from the Science of Learning
author: James M. Lang
description: Introduces minor, low-stakes changes to course design and classroom routines that produce major learning gains through cognitive science.

title: Designing Your Life: How to Build a Well-Lived, Joyful Life
author: Bill Burnett, Dave Evans
description: Stanford d.school professors show how design thinking can help you prototype careers and build a life that is creatively fulfilling and productive.

title: Excellent Sheep: The Miseducation of the American Elite and the Way to a Meaningful Life
author: William Deresiewicz
description: Former Yale professor critiques the hyper-competitive admissions treadmill that produces risk-averse students, advocating for genuine liberal arts self-discovery.

title: Creative Schools: The Grassroots Revolution That’s Transforming Education
author: Sir Ken Robinson, Lou Aronica
description: Sir Ken Robinson expands on his legendary TED Talk, offering a blueprint for transforming our industrial-style testing systems into personalized creative learning.

title: Teaching to Transgress: Education as the Practice of Freedom
author: bell hooks
description: bell hooks speaks to the heart of education as a liberating act, sharing strategies for creating engaged, passionate classrooms that transgress boundaries.

title: Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat: Mastering the Elements of Good Cooking
author: Samin Nosrat
description: Master the four basic elements of flavor and texture to cook delicious dishes with confidence without needing strict recipe formulas.

title: The Food Lab: Better Home Cooking Through Science
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
description: James Beard Award winner investigating culinary science and food chemistry to perfect cooking steaks, eggs, roasts, and vegetables at home.

title: Born to Run: A Hidden Tribe, Superathletes, and the Greatest Race the World Has Never Seen
author: Christopher McDougall
description: An exhilarating adventure tracking Mexico’s secretive Tarahumara Indians, who run hundreds of miles without injury, uncovering the secrets of human endurance.

title: The Omnivore’s Dilemma: A Natural History of Four Meals
author: Michael Pollan
description: Michael Pollan investigates the fundamental question: What should we have for dinner? Tracing industrial agriculture, organic farms, and hunter-gatherer meals.

title: In Defense of Food: An Eater’s Manifesto
author: Michael Pollan
description: Eat food. Not too much. Mostly plants. Pollan’s seven-word answer to the complexities of modern industrialized nutrition and processed foods.

title: How to Change Your Mind: What the New Science of Psychedelics Teaches Us
author: Michael Pollan
description: A brilliant immersion into the renaissance of scientific research into psychedelics and their clinical efficacy for depression, addiction, and terminal anxiety.

title: An Immense World: How Animal Senses Reveal the Hidden Realms Around Us
author: Ed Yong
description: Pulitzer Prize winner Ed Yong takes us beyond the limits of human senses into animal Umwelt, exploring echolocation, magnetic fields, and infrared visions.

title: I Contain Multitudes: The Microbes Within Us and a Grander View of Life
author: Ed Yong
description: A groundbreaking, tour of the microscopic organisms that shape human health, construct immune systems, and determine animal evolution.

title: The Architecture of Happiness
author: Alain de Botton
description: Alain de Botton explores how buildings, furniture, and interior architecture communicate values and directly influence our emotions and wellbeing.

title: Understanding Comics: The Invisible Art
author: Scott McCloud
description: The comic-book format masterclass exploring visual communication, panel transitions, closure, time frames, and the semiotics of graphic storytelling.

title: Ways of Seeing
author: John Berger
description: Based on the BBC television series, John Berger’s classic analyzes how our perception of art, women, property, and advertising is conditioned by cultural history.

title: The Design of Everyday Things: Revised and Expanded Edition
author: Don Norman
description: Cognitive scientist Don Norman explores user-centered design, signifiers, affordances, feedback, and why confusing door handles are faults of bad design.

title: On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft
author: Stephen King
description: Part memoir, part masterclass by one of the bestselling authors of all time, sharing invaluable practical tools on character, dialogue, pacing, and perseverance.

title: Bird by Bird: Some Instructions on Writing and Life
author: Anne Lamott
description: Anne Lamott shares wise, funny, and deeply honest advice on conquering writer’s block, writing terrible first drafts, and taking creative life bird by bird.

title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance: An Inquiry into Values
author: Robert M. Pirsig
description: A motorcycle journey across the American Northwest becomes a profound meditation on the Metaphysics of Quality, technology, craftsmanship, and human sanity.

title: Letters to a Young Poet
author: Rainer Maria Rilke
description: Rilke’s ten timeless letters to Franz Xaver Kappus on solitude, love, nature, artistic calling, and finding patience in life’s unanswerable questions.
